q: In the experiment-platform project, what do we know about q-ep-peeking-policy?
a: It asks whether teams may check A/B results daily and stop early. A/A simulation showed daily unadjusted looks push the false positive rate to 14 percent against a nominal 5 percent, so dec-ep-fixed-horizon allows one readout at the planned end.

q: In the experiment-platform project, what came of exp-502, the sample ratio mismatch audit?
a: Four of 38 tests failed SRM at p below 0.001, all caused by a bot filter applied only in treatment. That led to fnd-srm-bots and to dec-ep-srm-gate, which blocks readouts when SRM fails.

q: In the experiment-platform project, what does ep-cuped-v2 use as covariates?
a: feat-ep-pre-spend-cov-v2 (spend over 28 days ending 7 days before assignment) and feat-ep-prior-logins-14d. It replaced ep-cuped-v1, which used only the v1 pre-spend covariate.

q: In the experiment-platform project, what is the current default variance-reduction method for readouts?
a: CUPED v2 (ep-cuped-v2), set as the default by dec-ep-cuped-v2 on 2025-12-05. ep-cuped-v1 stays available only to reproduce older readouts.

q: In the experiment-platform project, what was the median variance reduction of CUPED v2 against v1 across the 12 finished tests?
a: 27 percent for CUPED v2 against 18 percent for v1, across 12 finished onboarding and marketing tests (exp-505, 2025-12-01).

q: In the experiment-platform project, why did we stop allowing early stops on daily looks?
a: A/A simulations showed 14 percent false positives with daily unadjusted peeks (exp-503), so dec-ep-fixed-horizon replaced dec-ep-daily-looks with a single readout at the planned end.
